on_screen_item: Label A QUAKER FAMILY
evidence: Britannica: 'born into a Quaker family'; Lonsdale p.99: mother fears she 'can never show myself at meeting in them'

on_screen_item: Real printed page of Quaker advice with 'plainness' highlighted; source chip
evidence: 1783 Extracts from the Minutes and Advices of the Yearly Meeting of Friends held in London, p.185, heading 'PLAINNESS': 'ADVISED that friends take care to keep to truth and plainness, in language, habit, deportment, and behaviour; that the simplicity of truth in these things may not wear out or be lost in our days, nor in our posterity's. To avoid pride and immodesty in apparel, and all vain and superfluous fashions of the world. 1691. P. E.' (P.E. = printed epistle)
suggested_wording: Use this page (archive.org leaf n198; 1783 printing, public domain by age; scan is a microfilm copy with black border). Highlight 'plainness, in language, habit' on line 1. Source chip: LONDON YEARLY MEETING ADVICE, 1691 · PRINTED IN 'EXTRACTS', 1783, P.185. Bonus on the same page: the 1703 advice warns against 'all extravagancy in colour and fashion', which sets up the mother's 'bright colour' complaint in the stockings story.

on_screen_item: Quote line PLAIN CLOTHES · PLAIN WORDS beside the page
evidence: The page says 'plainness, in language, habit, deportment, and behaviour'; the words 'plain clothes, plain words' are not on it
suggested_wording: Do not style it as a quotation next to the source. Either set it as a plain label without quote marks (PLAIN CLOTHES · PLAIN WORDS), or quote the page: 'PLAINNESS, IN LANGUAGE, HABIT…' (1691).

on_screen_item: Title page of Meteorological Observations and Essays (1793; Wellcome Collection, public domain)
evidence: Wellcome's openly digitised copies (Public Domain Mark) are the 1834 second edition (works xney7nyg, ny5z5tzn); its 1793 record (ey77thr6) is only a licensed ECCO e-book. A public-domain scan of the 1793 first edition is at ETH-Bibliothek Zürich (e-rara), 'Printed for W. Richardson, 1793', Public Domain Mark, DOI 10.3931/e-rara-3543
suggested_wording: Source the 1793 title page from e-rara (ETH-Bibliothek Zürich, Rar 5123, Public Domain Mark). Credit: 'Dalton 1793 · ETH-Bibliothek Zürich / e-rara'. If you use Wellcome, it must be labelled 1834 (2nd edition).

on_screen_item: Label THE DIARY · 1787 TO 1844 on the 1793 title page
evidence: The 1793 book cannot contain 1787-1844; Henry pp.11-12 describe a separate manuscript journal begun 'March 24, 1787' and 'continued ... in unbroken sequence to the evening before his decease'. The book prints five years of observations: 'at Kendal and Keswick for 5 years, from 1788 to 1792' (1834 reprint of 1793 text)
suggested_wording: On the title page use: HIS FIRST BOOK · 1793. Keep THE DIARY · 1787 TO 1844 for A2-10 only, and put it on a different visual (e.g. a written journal page; John Rylands Library holds surviving Dalton manuscripts incl. some meteorological records, many damaged in the 24 Dec 1940 Lit & Phil fire - check licence), or on a plain card/timeline, not on the printed book.

on_screen_item: Label HIS WEATHER RECORD on the 1793 title page
evidence: The book is a printed work of observations and essays; its tables come from his Kendal weather records 1788-1792 (with Crosthwaite's at Keswick), not the lifelong diary. Contents: 'Account of observations on the Barometer at Kendal and Keswick, for five years'
suggested_wording: BUILT ON HIS WEATHER RECORDS (or FIVE YEARS OF KENDAL WEATHER, 1788-92). Avoid anything that makes the book look like the diary.

on_screen_item: Mono tag THE DIARY · 1787 TO 1844
evidence: Henry pp.11-12: 'Observations upon the Weather, &c. &c, March 24, 1787 ... continued with steady perseverance in unbroken sequence to the evening before his decease' (died 27 July 1844)
suggested_wording: Fine as a tag, but not over the 1793 title page (see A2-08).

on_screen_item: Tag EVERY DAY · TO THE NIGHT BEFORE HE DIED
evidence: Henry p.12: 'in unbroken sequence to the evening before his decease'; Henry pp.198-199: last entry Friday 26 July
suggested_wording: Optional, closer to source: EVERY DAY · TO THE EVENING BEFORE HE DIED.

on_screen_item: Dateline KENDAL · LAKE DISTRICT
evidence: Spoken line says 'on the edge of the Lake District'; Kendal lies just outside the Lake District National Park and was in Westmorland
suggested_wording: KENDAL · WESTMORLAND (matches EAGLESFIELD · CUMBERLAND) or KENDAL · EDGE OF THE LAKE DISTRICT.

on_screen_item: Route Eaglesfield to Kendal
evidence: Henry p.4: 'In the year 1781, being then fifteen years old, he left Eaglesfield for Kendal'

on_screen_item: Tag TEACHING FROM AGE 15
evidence: Dalton's own note (Henry p.2): 'began about twelve to teach the village school, and continued it two years ... removed to Kendal at fifteen years of age as assistant in a boarding-school'; Henry p.4: 'At the age of twelve ... he actually commenced a school in his native village'
suggested_wording: IN KENDAL FROM AGE 15 (or TEACHING IN KENDAL FROM AGE 15). As written, the tag says he started teaching at 15; he started at about 12 in Eaglesfield.

on_screen_item: Label THE GERANIUM, 1792
evidence: Dalton 1798 p.29: 'the flower of the Geranium zonale by candle-light, in the Autumn of 1792'; Henry: kept school at Kendal to 1793
suggested_wording: Optional: THE GERANIUM · AUTUMN 1792. Plant in SRC-013 should be a pink Pelargonium zonale (factcheck2 a1-02).

on_screen_item: Colour eases to dark blue-grey; label JOHN'S VIEW
evidence: Lonsdale p.99: 'appeared to his eyes a bluish dark drab' - the biographer's words, not a measurement. Dalton himself (1798 p.33) says red things look very different to him, e.g. blood 'not unlike that colour called bottle-green'; Hunt et al. 1995 found he was a deuteranope. A blue-grey render labelled JOHN'S VIEW reads as what he actually saw
suggested_wording: Label: IN JOHN'S WORDS (or AS JOHN DESCRIBED IT), with REPORTED COLOURS visible. Avoid JOHN'S VIEW.

on_screen_item: Quote tag 'A BLUISH DARK DRAB' (Lonsdale 1874)
evidence: Lonsdale p.99: 'the colour of the said stockings appeared to his eyes a bluish dark drab, and quakerish enough in all verity'
suggested_wording: Verbatim; attribution to Lonsdale correct (not Dalton's own words).

on_screen_item: Label HIS MOTHER; same shot (still under KENDAL dateline)
evidence: Lonsdale p.99: 'On his next visit to Eaglesfield, the compliment of the stockings was duly made'
suggested_wording: The present is opened in Eaglesfield, not Kendal. Add dateline EAGLESFIELD on 'His mother opens the present', or drop the KENDAL dateline before this beat.

on_screen_item: Quote 'AS RED AS A CHERRY'
evidence: Lonsdale p.99: '"They're as red as a cherry, John!" But John could not see this'. Her first words were '...what made thee fancy such a bright colour?'
suggested_wording: Verbatim. Optional full line: "THEY'RE AS RED AS A CHERRY, JOHN!"

on_screen_item: Back to dark; label JOHN
evidence: Lonsdale p.99: 'But John could not see this'
suggested_wording: Keep the REPORTED COLOURS tag.

on_screen_item: Label JONATHAN joins JOHN; both DARK, MOTHER RED
evidence: Lonsdale p.99: 'nor could brother Jonathan, who was also present; so there were two to one in the dispute'
suggested_wording: Lonsdale says only that Jonathan could not see the red and sided with John; 'DARK' for Jonathan is an inference, acceptable under REPORTED COLOURS.

on_screen_item: Labels JOHN · DARK, JONATHAN · DARK, MOTHER · RED
evidence: As A2-29/32/35; Lonsdale p.100 adds the neighbours' verdict 'varra fine stuff, but uncommon scarlety'

evidence: Dalton p.29-30: 'sky-blue by day; in candle-light ... being what I called red' - these are his colour names, not a record of what he saw
